title: ask-boarding-cadence-and-release-pressure-notes-2026-05-11
body:
TL;DR: early-adopter sites are flagging onboarding friction tied to cadence and release windows. Requests cluster into: (A) faster, lower-risk post-signup guidance (docs + templates + starter prompts), (B) explicit cost/latency expectations during trial, and (C) ability to pin a stable model variant during ramp. Quick wins identified (A1, B1) could be shipped in 2 sprints; larger asks (C) need eng + infra design.

Context & why this matters:
- Several mid-market customers paused their production rollouts citing frequent minor release/noise during ramp week. They report that even non-breaking changes to model selection, batch sizing, or default quantization profiles caused unpredictable token cost spikes.
- Onboarding velocity correlates to early retention: customers who completed the quick-start and saw a stable 95th percentile latency target within 7 days were 3x more likely to convert to Dedicated.
- This doc synthesizes raw feedback collected from onboarding calls (Apr–May 2026), support tickets, and two post-trial interviews. It focuses on actionable asks and suggested probes.

Raw customer excerpts (anonymized):
- "We built our first integration in 3 days, then a week later the model defaults changed and our per-conversation cost doubled — no heads up."
- "We want a sandbox with fixed model pins; can't risk the devs merging in a stealth quantized variant that breaks quality."
- "The quickstart is good but missing the 'what to expect' section: typical token counts, latency, and cost per path for small/med/large payloads."

Synthesis: request clusters and hypotheses
1) Predictability & release control (high impact, medium effort)
   - Request: ability for customers (trial & Hosted) to pin a model variant per-route or per-team for N days.
   - Hypothesis: Pinning reduces churn by avoiding surprise regressions; measurable via fewer support escalations within first 30 days.
   - Engineering considerations: config surface at route-level + backend enforcement + audit logs + UX for pin calendar. Possible interaction w/ auto-fallback policies.

2) Onboarding transparency (high impact, low effort)
   - Request: a short "what to expect" slab added to quickstart showing: median/95p latency, token cost examples, and common payload sizes.
   - Hypothesis: clarity reduces triage tickets and speeds up conversion.
   - Quick fixes: add a one-pager + inline examples in SDK snippets; annotate model catalog with expected token-cost bands.

3) Trial-mode cost-guard (medium impact, medium effort)
   - Request: an opt-in cost-guard for trials that caps per-request or per-day spend and returns structured error with guidance when hit.
   - Hypothesis: customers will feel safer experimenting and less likely to convert to Dedicated if surprised by bills.

4) Release-telemetry nudges (medium impact, low effort)
   - Request: automated email/console notifications when a model default or routing policy that affects the account changes.
   - Hypothesis: proactive communication reduces surprised escalations and improves CS handoffs.

Prioritization table (rough):
- A: Onboarding transparency (B1) => priority P0, owner: CS docs + DevX (2-week turnaround)
- B: Release-notice nudges => priority P1, owner: Console + Notifications (1 sprint small eng task)
- C: Trial cost-guard => priority P1, owner: Billing + Platform (1–2 sprints)
- D: Model pinning per-route => priority P2, owner: Serving Runtime + Console (R&D + API design; 6–10 wks)

Proposed experiments / small bets to validate quickly:
- Experiment 1: Add a small "expected cost and latency" block to the quickstart and monitor: support tickets mentioning "cost surprise", trial-to-paid spike, and time-to-first-successful-request. (owner: Maya / Priya)
- Experiment 2: Send a 'release preview' digest to 15 active trial accounts before a small routing change; measure follow-up engagement and ticket count. (owner: Ethan)

Engineering notes & blockers (from sync with infra + runtime):
- The runtime currently allows variant fallthroughs for performance; adding hard pins will require a 'pin layer' in routing that bypasses automatic fallback unless explicitly allowed — non-trivial for autoscaling edge cases.
- Audit logs exist but need a better mapping to customer-visible timeline UI.
- Billing team: need a safe-path for trial cost-guard (refund semantics? overage prevents conversion?)

Metrics to watch (baseline + targets):
- Number of trial escalations mentioning "unexpected cost" (target: -50% in 8 weeks with transparency docs)
- 30-day conversion rate for newly onboarded customers who receive the quickstart update (target: +15% relative lift)
- Support L2 time spent on post-release triage (target: 25% reduction)

Suggested copy snippets (to paste into quickstart):
- "What to expect: Typical payloads and costs
  - Short chat ( <= 200 tokens input, <= 400 tokens output): median latency ~120ms, cost ~ $0.003 per call
  - Long summarization (3–5k tokens): median latency ~1.1s, cost ~ $0.12 per call
  - These are illustrative; your workload may vary — see Console -> Model profiler for per-route breakdowns."

Action plan (next 30 days):
- Week 1: ship quickstart transparency block + update model catalog tags (owner: DevX docs).
- Week 2: implement console-level release-notice toggle and pilot with 15 accounts (owner: Console eng).
- Week 3–4: spec trial cost-guard and collect legal/billing feedback (owner: Billing + CS).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should pins be enforceable for Hosted tier or only for Dedicated/private? (ops risk tradeoffs).
- Refund policy for trial cost-guard breaches — instant rollback or credit? (billing/legal)
- UX: should model pins be time-limited by default? (affects rollout complexity)

Notes-to-self / meeting snippets:
- 2026-05-12 sync: infra worried about pining + autoscaler interplay; propose dev sandbox for pin tests.
- 2026-05-13: Priya to draft customer-facing FAQ for ‘why defaults change’
- TODO: attach sample tickets and two anonymized call transcripts (Ethan)

Appendix: sample support ticket summaries (short)
- TKT-3219: Customer X reported sudden cost increase after a minor rollout to defaults. Cause: a routing tweak moved them from a cached hot-path to a fallback variant for ~12h.
- TKT-3244: Customer Y wanted a 'no-change' window during their ramp week; asked for calendar pinning capability.

If you want to run a quick prioritization workshop, propose: 30-min async vote (impact x effort) in the CS channel, then a 1-hr sync with Console/Product to align owners.

----
End of doc (working). Will iterate after DevX + Console responses.
